text:
Elena: customer reports function-calling failing with schema error after migrating to our OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Error from runtime: `invalid_arguments: expected Object for 'arguments' but got String`. They pasted the model response: 

```json
{
  "name": "create_ticket",
  "arguments": "{\"title\":\"Login failure\",\"urgency\":\"low-priority\"}"
}
```

Elena: repro steps they sent:
1) call /v1/chat/completions with function spec
2) model returns `function_call` with `arguments` as a stringified JSON
3) our tool-exec path tries to validate the arguments against the schema and rejects it.

Elena: customer is blocked (billing escalated). Any quick ideas? :thinking_face:

Raj: I can reproduce. This is a common divergence — some OpenAI-compatible models return `arguments` as a string. The official spec expects JSON object but not every model follows it. Our parser currently enforces object type strictly.

Raj: two options: 1) ask customers to normalize (not great), or 2) make our parser tolerant: if `arguments` is a string, attempt JSON.parse when it looks like JSON. Need product/security sign-off.

Devon: auto-parsing seems reasonable but watch out for big payloads and injection patterns. Also impacts caching/deduping: string vs object changes canonicalization. We should normalize before caching. Add telemetry for changed shape.

Elena: customer needs a workaround now. Can we tell them to add a step to parse the returned arguments on their side? They are using a third-party model host and can't change model behavior.

Raj: quick repro I ran locally:
```bash
# simulated response body from model
RESP='{"name":"create_ticket","arguments":"{"title":"Login failure","urgency":"low-priority"}"}'
# current parser fails when expecting object
# proposed tolerant parse snippet (pseudocode)
if typeof(resp.arguments) == 'string' and resp.arguments.trim().startsWith('{') then
  parsed = JSON.parse(resp.arguments)
else
  parsed = resp.arguments
end
```

Raj: also noticed enum mismatch: our tool schema expects urgency in ["low","medium","high"] but caller/model used "low-priority". I'll add a small synonyms map for known enums during normalization.

Devon: rollout plan: feature-flag the tolerant parser + enum aliasing. Canary 10% for 24h, monitor error/firehose and latency. If parsing fails or throws, fall back to rejecting to avoid silent corruption.

OpsBot: created canary flag `ff_toolcall_tolerant_args`. Canary job: job/ff-toolcall-tolerant-args created. Link: https://deploys.redwood.internal/jobs/ff-toolcall-tolerant-args

Elena: told customer we'll ship a hotfix behind a flag and give them a timeline (ETA 48h). Also gave them a temporary client-side snippet to parse the stringified arguments.

Raj: opening PR with tests + telemetry. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124 (draft). Includes: tolerant parse, enum alias map, unit tests, and a flag.

Devon: once PR is ready, I'll schedule canary deploy and add automated rollback if error rate > 1% or latency regression > 50ms.

Elena: marking the ticket as escalated -> eng-oncall looped. Will update customer after canary. :white_check_mark:

Raj: small follow-up — we should add a logged sample (redacted) when we auto-parse so support can proactively contact other customers affected. Add a telemetry tag `toolcall_arg_shape_fix_applied`.

Devon: agreed. Also add a rate limit on auto-parse attempts per org to avoid noisy logs.

Elena: thanks team. I'll attach the customer's conversation to the ticket and close the loop once canary is green.

(opsbot): deployment scheduled for 2025-11-03 03:00 UTC — will monitor.
